newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end weaker, pare early losses.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end weaker, pare early losses.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei stock index futures pared early losses but ended weaker on Monday, tracking the currency market fluctuations of dollar/yen, dealers said.
"Sentiment improved during the latter half on yen sales," a Japanese commission house dealer said, noting a rebound in Tokyo stocks as the yen's rising momentum against the dollar ebbed.
The dollar/yen rate recovered from a dip to the 119 level on demand from Japanese investors and importers in mid-afternoon.
March Nikkei futures ended lower at 18,405 points, down 185 points from Friday, but off the session's low at 18,310. A total of 28,980 contracts changed hands.
Dealers said the cash Nikkei's plummet on Friday, and three consecutive days of losses on Wall Street, cast a dark cloud over futures trading, and could guide prices lower this week.
The yen's strength against the dollar was also construed as unhelpful to Japanese exports and stock prices, dealers said.
"Investors are generally avoiding Japanese stocks. Anything lower than 18,300 points is going to be bad news," another dealer with a European house said.
Nikkei futures were seen likely to re-test support at 18,300 points and to be resisted heavily around 18,550 points.
